description: A simple, stable-knowledge question that never requires web_search.
input: What is the capital of France?

assistant.content: The capital of France is Paris.

description: A factual, current-information question that requires exactly one web_search call.
input: What is the latest stable version of Python?

results.title: Python Releases
results.snippet: Python 3.13 is the latest stable release.

assistant.content: The latest stable version of Python is 3.13 (see https://www.python.org/downloads/).

description: A comparison question where the agent must search once per compared item before answering.
input: Compare current backend adoption of Rust vs Go in production systems.

results.title: Rust in production
results.snippet: Rust adoption is growing in performance-critical backends.

results.title: Go in production
results.snippet: Go remains widely adopted for cloud-native backend services.

assistant.content: Both are widely used: Rust is growing in performance-critical services (example.com/rust-adoption), while Go remains a common default for cloud-native backends (example.com/go-adoption).

description: web_search executes successfully but returns an empty result list; the agent must acknowledge the limitation.
input: What did the fictional city of Nowhereville announce at its 2099 tech summit?

assistant.content: I could not find any sources about this event; it may not exist or is not indexed. I cannot answer this reliably.

description: web_search raises an exception (simulated network failure); the agent must recover and still produce a bounded answer.
input: What is today's exchange rate for the fictional XYZ currency?

tool_calls.error: Simulated network timeout while contacting the search provider.

assistant.content: The search tool failed, so I cannot verify a current exchange rate for XYZ. Please retry later or provide a currency converter source.

description: An ambiguous question with no resolvable subject; the agent should ask for clarification instead of guessing or searching blindly.

assistant.content: Your question is too vague for me to research. Could you clarify what topic, person, or event you mean by 'it'?

description: The user asks for several distinct facts in one question; the agent should gather them via a focused search and report all of them.
input: What are the capital, population, and official language of Japan?

results.title: Japan - Country Profile
results.snippet: Capital: Tokyo. Population: ~123 million. Official language: Japanese.

assistant.content: Japan's capital is Tokyo, its population is approximately 123 million, and its official language is Japanese (example.com/japan).

description: The agent keeps requesting searches and never reaches a final answer within the configured turn budget.
input: Research an open-ended topic that requires endless follow-up verification.

description: Search results across two queries disagree; the agent must present both sides rather than pick one arbitrarily.
input: Is coffee good or bad for health?

results.title: Coffee linked to lower disease risk
results.snippet: A large cohort study found moderate coffee intake reduces certain disease risks.

results.title: Coffee linked to increased anxiety and sleep issues
results.snippet: Another review found high coffee intake worsens anxiety and sleep quality.

assistant.content: Evidence is mixed: some studies (example.com/coffee-good) associate moderate coffee intake with lower disease risk, while others (example.com/coffee-bad) link high intake to worse anxiety and sleep. Moderation appears key, and individual response varies.

description: A multi-dimensional comparison question that requires more than one search but completes normally with a grounded final answer.
input: Which is more suitable for building AI agents: Python or TypeScript, considering ecosystem, tooling, and deployment?

results.title: Python AI ecosystem
results.snippet: Python has mature AI/ML libraries and agent frameworks.

results.title: TypeScript AI tooling
results.snippet: TypeScript offers strong tooling and deployment ergonomics for web-facing agents.

assistant.content: Python is generally more suitable due to its mature AI/ML ecosystem (example.com/python-ai), while TypeScript offers stronger tooling for web-deployed agent front-ends (example.com/typescript-ai). Choice depends on whether the priority is ML/data work or web integration.
